## Solution

We want
$$L = \lim_{n\to\infty}\left(\prod_{j=2}^{n}\bigl((2j-1)!!\bigr)^{1/j}\right)^{1/n^{2}}.$$

**Indexing.** The displayed product is $\sqrt{3!!}\cdot\sqrt[3]{5!!}\cdots\sqrt[n]{(2n-1)!!}$. The factor with root index $j$ (for $j=2,\dots,n$) carries the value $(2j-1)!!$, since $j=2\mapsto 3!!$, $j=3\mapsto 5!!$, $j=n\mapsto(2n-1)!!$. Hence
$$P_n:=\prod_{j=2}^{n}\bigl((2j-1)!!\bigr)^{1/j},\qquad L=\lim_{n\to\infty}P_n^{1/n^{2}}.$$

**Logarithmic form.** Set $S_n:=\log P_n=\sum_{j=2}^{n}\frac{1}{j}\log\bigl((2j-1)!!\bigr)$. Then $\log L=\lim_{n\to\infty}S_n/n^{2}$.

**Asymptotics of $\log((2j-1)!!)$.** Using $(2j-1)!!=(2j)!/(2^{j}j!)$ and Stirling's formula $\log m!=m\log m-m+\tfrac12\log(2\pi m)+O(1/m)$:
$$\log((2j)!)=2j\log(2j)-2j+\tfrac12\log(4\pi j)+O(1/j),$$
$$\log(j!)=j\log j-j+\tfrac12\log(2\pi j)+O(1/j).$$
Subtracting (with the $-j\log 2$ from the $2^{j}$):
$$\log((2j-1)!!)=j\log 2+j\log j-j+\tfrac12\log 2+O(1/j).$$
Therefore
$$\frac{1}{j}\log((2j-1)!!)=\log 2+\log j-1+O(1/j).$$

**Summing.**
$$S_n=\sum_{j=2}^{n}\bigl(\log 2+\log j-1\bigr)+\sum_{j=2}^{n}O(1/j).$$
The error sum is $O(\log n)$. For the main part,
$$\sum_{j=2}^{n}(\log 2-1)=(n-1)(\log 2-1),\qquad \sum_{j=2}^{n}\log j=\log(n!).$$
Using $\log(n!)=n\log n-n+\tfrac12\log(2\pi n)+O(1/n)$:
$$S_n=(n-1)(\log 2-1)+n\log n-n+\tfrac12\log(2\pi n)+O(\log n)$$
$$=n\log n+n\log 2-2n+O(\log n)=n\log(2n)-2n+O(\log n).$$

**The limit.**
$$\frac{S_n}{n^{2}}=\frac{n\log(2n)-2n+O(\log n)}{n^{2}}=\frac{\log(2n)-2}{n}+O\!\left(\frac{\log n}{n^{2}}\right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}0.$$

Hence $\log L=0$, and
$$\boxed{L=e^{0}=1}.$$

**Sanity check.** $P_n\sim \exp\bigl(n\log(2n)-2n\bigr)=(2n)^{n}e^{-2n}$, so $P_n^{1/n^{2}}=(2n)^{1/n}e^{-2/n}\to 1\cdot 1=1$, confirming the result.
